extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literature, history, and character-writing interested in theories of heroism (general educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for depicting or evaluating 'great men' / heroes in literature and history, drawn from Carlyle's lectures on heroism: what makes a hero authentically great, how they relate to society and religion, and how they inspire worship and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: History as Biography of Great Men
rubrics_metrics.description: Universal History is at bottom the History of the Great Men who have worked here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carlyle argues that the outer accomplishments of the world are the practical realization and embodiment of Thoughts that dwelt in Great Men; when evaluating or creating a hero, emphasize their causal role in shaping events and institutions rather than treating them as incidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Man as 'living light-fountain' (original insight and noble manhood)
rubrics_metrics.description: A great man is profitable company, a 'living light-fountain' of native original insight, of manhood and heroic nobleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray the hero as a source of illumination: original perceptions, moral strength, and an unmistakable nobility of character that others gravitate toward. Show their insight concretely through decisions and speech rather than mere reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion (practical belief) as chief fact
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's religion is the primary fact about him — not merely creeds he professes but the thing he practically believes and acts upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a convincing hero, make clear his operative convictions — what he truly believes about duty, destiny, the unseen. These lived beliefs should causally determine his actions and decisions in narrative or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity over Quackery or Mere Allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Religions and hero-figures were not born of quackery or playful allegory; their origin is rooted in real felt truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making heroes appear as mere rhetorical constructs or fraudulent figures. Even when symbolic, their authority must be grounded in genuine conviction or lived experience; allegorical elements should arise from that certainty, not replace it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero as Embodiment of the Divine or Highest Human
rubrics_metrics.description: Man is 'the true Shekinah' — the Highest Being reveals himself in man; Hero-worship reflects reverence for the divine in man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting a hero, emphasize qualities that make them emblematic of the highest human or divine attributes (moral intensity, sacrificial stature, prophetic presence). The hero functions as a visible revelation of higher realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to Arouse Transcendent Admiration (Hero-worship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hero-worship is 'transcendent admiration' — boundless submission and reverence for a noblest godlike Form of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A true hero should inspire deep, sometimes devotional, admiration in others. Show the effects of that admiration (loyalty, obedience, social cohesion) in character interactions and social consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive, Salvific Leadership in Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: The Great Man is the 'indispensable savior of his epoch' — the lightning that kindles the dry fuel of a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatize or demonstrate the hero's ability to diagnose the needs of an era and act decisively to change its course. Heroic action should have palpable, epoch-making consequences within the story or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Merely 'Creature of the Time' (individual agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Great men are not merely the product or 'creature' of their times; they possess personal agency that is not wholly explainable as the Time's effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the hero individuality and initiative; resist reducing them to deterministic historical forces. Show choices and convictions that distinguish them from contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of Wisdom to Discern and Valor to Lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Wisdom to discern truly what the Time wanted, and valor to lead it on the right road thither, are the salvation of any Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct heroes who pair intellectual or moral insight with courage and willingness to act. Scenes should illustrate both discernment (seeing what is needed) and courageous execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero as Generator of Loyalty and Social Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Society is founded on Hero-worship: all dignities of rank and the life-breath of society are effluences of admiration for the great.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When showing a hero's social role, highlight how their presence organizes social hierarchies, loyalties, and institutions. The hero's authority should legitimize or reorder communal structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to Elevate Others by Reverence
rubrics_metrics.description: By revering what is truly above him, a true man is 'made higher'; reverence for a hero elevates those who worship him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict the reciprocal effect of heroism: followers are morally or spiritually lifted by their admiration. Use scenes of mentorship, transformation, or moral instruction to show this elevation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic Sensibility and Recognition of Beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: He that can discern the loveliness of things is called Poet; the power to see every object as 'a window into Infinitude' is a heroic/poetic trait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give heroes a perceptive, poetic awareness of nature and human beauty; such sensitivity helps mark them as exceptional. Use evocative imagery and moments of aesthetic insight to convey this trait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rootedness in Felt Reality that Produces Symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegory and symbol (religion, myth) are the products of prior certainty and felt reality, not their origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a hero becomes symbolic or mythic in a narrative, ensure the symbolic status grows from lived deeds and convictions, not from authorial imposition. Show experiences that organically give rise to legend or cult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity, Rustic Truthfulness, and Earnestness
rubrics_metrics.description: In praising Scandinavian Paganism Carlyle notes a 'broad simplicity, rusticity, homely truthfulness, a great rude sincerity' as virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider representing heroes with straightforward sincerity and unpretentious strength; an unadorned earnestness can be as powerful as cultivated eloquence. Avoid making sincerity merely a rhetorical mask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Personification/Impersonation to Convey Grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: Scandinavian mythology 'impersonates' forces of Nature as personal agencies (gods, jotuns) — a way to render the stupendous as alive and relational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creative depiction, personify large forces (fate, nature, social upheaval) in relation to the hero to dramatize stakes and scale. Such personification should clarify the hero's confrontation with vast impersonal powers.
